expectations.text: Asks no questions: the final message contains no question to the user, no options to choose from and no request to review or approve
expectations.evidence: final_message.md is a 4-sentence report with no question, options or review request; ends 'Es gibt keine Konflikte mit den Anforderungen.'

expectations.text: Traceability: every story/acceptance criterion and every business rule of the target requirements document is mapped to a concrete design element
expectations.evidence: 002-task-reminders.md 'Traceability' table has rows for S1.1-S1.7, S2.1-S2.6, S3.1-S3.6, S4.1-S4.3 and R1-R12, each tied to a design element and a test ID. The worked examples T-PLAN-1..18 are correct when checked (e.g. S1.3 'A due Wed 2026-01-07 (Tue 01-06 is Epiphany)... no pre-due reminder'; S3.5 re-notice on Tue 10-06).

expectations.text: No open decisions: the design contains no TBD/TODO, no 'either X or Y' left to developers, no unresolved 'consider'/'if needed' choices
expectations.evidence: grep finds no TBD/TODO/consider/if needed. The conditionals that remain resolve to one answer, e.g. 'If the existing detail route/API restricts it to the assignee, allow MEISTER for all tasks'. Every choice (luxon, react-onesignal, injectManifest, 07:59 window) is stated as decided.

expectations.text: Out-of-scope items of the target requirements are not designed or built
expectations.evidence: Traceability lists each out-of-scope item as 'Not built'. There is no settings screen ('No settings screen (Out of scope)'). /overview is reused with no overdue view. Tasks assigned to a MEISTER produce no reminder (T-PLAN-18). There is no email fallback ('NO_DEVICE logged, no other channel').

expectations.text: Data model given with entities, fields and types; API/interfaces given with method, path and request/response shape
expectations.evidence: Field tables for PushSubscription, ReminderRun and ReminderMessage (types, nullability, defaults, @@unique([runDate, recipientId, kind])). 'PUT /api/push-subscriptions/:subscriptionId' with body '{ "userAgent"?: string }' returns '204'. The DELETE endpoint is specified too. The OneSignal POST request body and the response-to-status mapping are given.

expectations.text: All written files are in English
expectations.evidence: 002-task-reminders.md, ADRs 0005-0007 and the overview.md additions are in English. The only German text is the push and UI strings, which QE2 requires. final_message.md is German, but it is the chat reply, not a repo file.

expectations.text: Stays on the existing stack (NestJS/TypeScript, Prisma, PostgreSQL, React PWA) and introduces no new language or database
expectations.evidence: 'New api dependencies: @nestjs/schedule ^4, luxon ^3 ... New web dependency: react-onesignal ^3'. 'No new process or container'. There is no new database or language.

expectations.text: Uses OneSignal for push as the stakeholder stated, including how devices/users are registered (e.g. external user id = Taskli user id)
expectations.evidence: ADR 0005 chooses OneSignal Web Push. For registration, the PWA sends 'PUT /api/push-subscriptions/<id>' with the OneSignal subscription id, the api stores it against the authenticated user and sends with 'include_subscription_ids'. External ids are deliberately not used, with a stated security reason ('a client could claim another user's id').

expectations.text: The 07:00 trigger is defined in Europe/Berlin although the server runs in UTC, and DST transitions are handled
expectations.evidence: "@Cron('*/5 7 * * *', { timeZone: 'Europe/Berlin' ...})" and '05:00 UTC in summer, 06:00 UTC in winter'. Test T-CAL-3 checks '2026-03-30T05:00Z and 2026-10-26T06:00Z are both 07:00 local'; both are correct for the 2026 DST dates.

expectations.text: Bavarian holidays are computed per year including Easter-based movable holidays and exclude 15 Aug and 8 Aug
expectations.evidence: 'bavarianHolidays(y)' = the 7 fixed dates plus E-2/E+1/E+39/E+50/E+60, using the Meeus/Jones/Butcher formula written out in the doc. 'Not holidays: 15 Aug, 8 Aug'. The table of Easter dates for 2026-2030 is correct (checked).

expectations.text: The daily run is idempotent: a restart or duplicate run never sends a second message to a person on the same day (persisted record)
expectations.evidence: ReminderRun has runDate as @id. ReminderMessage has @@unique([runDate, recipientId, kind]). 'a row once SENT, NO_DEVICE or FAILED is never sent again'. The OneSignal idempotency_key equals the row id, which covers a crash between send and status update (T-RUN-3, T-RUN-4).

expectations.text: Behaviour after a missed 07:00 run (server down) is defined and consistent with R2/R8
expectations.evidence: The behaviour is defined: catch-up until 07:59, then the day is dropped. It is not consistent with R8. Assumption A1 says the catch-up message has 'content as at that moment (not as at 07:00)', so tasks created or assigned between 07:00 and the catch-up are included, although R8 says such tasks are 'only considered from the next regular 07:00'. ADR 0006 claims 'This keeps R2 ... and R8', which contradicts A1.

expectations.text: Meister notice is sent once per task, persisted, and can re-trigger after a due-date change (R10)
expectations.evidence: 'workingDaysOverdue(due, today) == 2. Exactly 2 (not >= 2) ... a changed due date yields a new 2nd day and therefore a new notice'. The notice is persisted as a MEISTER_NOTICE row with taskIds and is unique per date. T-PLAN-12 and T-PLAN-15 cover both cases.

expectations.text: 'Today', 'tomorrow' and working-day overdue counting are computed in Europe/Berlin on date-only due dates
expectations.evidence: 'LocalDate = YYYY-MM-DD in Europe/Berlin. today = Berlin date of the run. Task.dueDate (@db.Date) is read as its YYYY-MM-DD value (... toISOString().slice(0, 10), never local-time getters)'. 'workingDaysOverdue' counts dates w with due < w <= today. T-CAL-3 checks the date at '2026-09-23T22:30Z is 2026-09-24'.

expectations.text: Tap targets specified: single task opens that task, multiple opens the employee list or the Meister overview
expectations.evidence: 'Employee message with exactly 1 task in total -> ${baseUrl}/tasks/<taskId>; >= 2 tasks -> ${baseUrl}/tasks'. 'Meister notice with exactly 1 task -> /tasks/<taskId>; >= 2 tasks -> /overview'. OneSignal is set to navigate on tap, and login keeps the target via 'next'.

notes: 1) Stronger security than a naive external_id approach: subscriptions are bound to the user on the server, so no client can claim another user's reminders (QE4). 2) The R8 deviation during catch-up is written down openly as assumption A1, but ADR 0006 still says the design 'keeps R8', which is a contradiction inside the docs. 3) ttl 43200 means a phone that is off at 07:00 can still show the message until 19:00. That is delivery rather than sending, but it stretches 'messages arrive at 07:00' and R8's 'nothing is sent during the day'. 4) The design is very detailed (dry-run CLI, CSP headers, a 'not available' state on task detail). Nothing out of scope is built, but the design is on the heavy side. 5) The eval set has no assertion on the security of push targeting; this run would have scored better on one.
